fields.meta_description: A conversational landing page asks one question per screen and branches on each answer. See four examples, then build your own by prompt.
fields.h1: Build a Conversational Landing Page, One Question at a Time
fields.hero_description: Build a conversational landing page that asks one question per screen, branches on answers, and saves replies to your database.
fields.features_subheading: Each screen asks one thing. The answer picks the next screen, lands in your database, and alerts a rep when a lead is worth a call.
fields.feature_1:
One question on each screen

Describe the questions in order, and Emergent builds a page that shows them one per screen, with a progress bar and a back button. Reword any of the questions later by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
The next question picked by the last answer

Name the answers that change the path, such as more than 50 employees. The page skips questions that do not apply and sends each visitor to the end screen their answers lead to.
fields.feature_3:
Every reply saved as a row

Each conversation lands as one row in a database you own, with every answer in its own column and the time it came in. Unfinished ones are saved too, up to the last answer given.
fields.feature_4:
A Slack message for leads that qualify

Set the answers that make a lead worth a call, and the rep who owns it gets a Slack message or an email with the answers. The app can also send each lead to any CRM with an API.
fields.feature_5:
Drop-off counted at each question

A dashboard shows how many visitors reached each question and how many left there. When one question loses more people than the others, you see which one and can move it or cut it.
fields.feature_6:
Hosted on your domain, or exported

Publish the page on your own domain; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep working on it there.
fields.why_title: Why Build Conversational Pages on Emergent?
fields.why_description: The questions, the branches, and the answer log live in one app you change by prompt. Adding a question takes one message.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every lead over 50 employees books with sales

Harborline Payroll asks four questions, one per screen. A company with more than 50 employees gets a calendar to book a sales call, and account executive Teo Marchetti gets a Slack message with the answers. Smaller companies get the free trial link. This week, 41 of 186 finished conversations went to sales.
fields.tab_content_2:
The phone question moved after it lost 31 visitors

Tallgrass Roofing in Omaha asks five questions before it quotes a job, and the phone number used to come second. This month, 300 visitors started and 214 finished. The dashboard showed the phone question losing 31 of the 86 who quit, more than any other. The owner made it optional and moved it to the last screen.
fields.tab_content_3:
One answer puts first-timers in Saturday's intro class

Pinecrest Climbing in Boulder opens with one question: New to climbing? A visitor who taps Yes is offered the Saturday 10:00 intro class, where 6 of 9 spots are taken, and books with a name and email. A visitor who taps No goes to a belay check booking. Each booking is saved with the answer.
fields.tab_content_4:
Three answers pick one of six samplers

Oakhollow Tea asks about caffeine, flavor, and brewing, one screen at a time. The answers point to one of six samplers. Low caffeine, floral, and loose leaf lead to Evening Garden, at $18. This month, 1,240 visitors answered all three questions, and 312 of them bought the sampler they were shown.

fields.hero_prompt: Build a conversational landing page for my payroll software that asks four questions and sends companies over 50 employees to a sales call.

faq_plan.q: What is a conversational landing page?
How do I create a conversational landing page?

plan.angle: The top 10 for this query is a mix of chatbot vendor blog posts (Intent Amplify, Mesh Agency), generic high-converting examples (Unbounce, Intercom), a Dribbble gallery of chat page designs, a funnel-versus-page post and a Reddit thread where a growth team worries that visitors dislike chat layouts. None shows the build: the question order, which answer sends a visitor down which branch, where the answers land, and which question loses people. This page shows four working conversational pages by goal (qualifying a lead, pricing a job, booking a first class, recommending a product), each with its branch rule and its numbers, plus how-to steps on question order, length and a plain-form fallback, and an FAQ on question count, chatbots, drop-off and CRM handoff.
tab_stories: Harborline Payroll asks four questions one at a time, and any company with more than 50 employees is offered a sales call while account executive Teo Marchetti gets a Slack message; smaller teams get the free trial link.

Tallgrass Roofing in Omaha asks five questions before a quote, and its dashboard showed the phone number question losing 31 of the 86 visitors who quit this month, so the phone question moved to an optional last step.

Pinecrest Climbing in Boulder opens with Have you climbed before?, sends first-timers to the Saturday 10:00 intro class with 6 of 9 spots taken, and sends experienced climbers to a belay check booking.
Oakhollow Tea asks three taste questions and shows one of six samplers, and 312 of the 1,240 visitors who answered all three this month bought the sampler they were shown.
